is_anopheles.evidence: Cone bioassays used susceptible Anopheles strains (Kisumu and Ngousso) to evaluate net bio-efficacy (page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No resistance markers were genotyped in this study. The paper only mentions 'no known kdr mutations' in reference to the susceptible Ngousso colony (page 3).

african_field_population.evidence: No field mosquitoes were tested; only laboratory susceptible colonies (Kisumu and Ngousso) were used in cone bioassays to test net insecticidal potency (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study assessing LLIN physical durability and residual bio-efficacy in Cameroon.

sub_country_location.evidence: Net sampling took place in Limbe, Tiko, and Buea in Fako division, Cameroon (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted 4 years after the 2011 campaign, around 2015-2016.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the physical integrity and insecticidal potency of LLINs retrieved from households in Cameroon using WHO cone bioassays with susceptible laboratory mosquito colonies (Kisumu and Ngousso). No wild mosquito populations were tested and no molecular resistance marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: No African field-caught mosquitoes tested (only laboratory susceptible colonies used for cone bioassays)
